text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- TREASURY EXPENSES DOUBLE ON DEBT INTEREST

The National Treasury paid 1.75 percent interest in reais in September on 107.1 billion reais in debt, with payments on interest alone totalling 1.223 billion reais, more than double the monthly average in the year's first half.
-- OIL IMPORTS SHOULD GROW 22 PERCENT THIS YEAR

Imports of oil and lubricants by Brazilian state oil firm Petrobras should grow by $1.2 billion, or roughly 22 percent, to $6.3 billion in 1996. Higher oil imports were behind a sharp rise in Brazil's trade deficit in September.
-- FORD BRASIL RAISES $300 MILLION VIA EUROBOND
Ford Brasil Ltda yesterday raised $300 million through the issue of an eight-year eurobond.
O GLOBO
-- FEDERAL BANK TO HELP FINANCE HOME BUYING, BUILDING

Brazil's government Oct 28 will launch a financial package aimed at aiding the middle class. Federal bank Caixa Economica Federal will use one billion reais to help finance the purchase, construction and remodeling of homes and apartments.
-- YELTSIN SACKS GENERAL LEBED FROM KREMLIN
Russian President Boris Yeltsin yesterday fired his National Security Secretary Gen. Alexander Lebed, accusing him of campaigning for the presidency.
-- GAS LEAK KILLS FOUR IN RIO'S COPACABANA NEIGHBORHOOD
A gas leak killed three children and the sister of the family's maid in an apartment in Rio de Janeiro's Copacabana neighborhood.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- BRAZIL'S TREASURY BLAMES STATES FOR DEFICIT

Brazil's National Treasury said loans to states are behind the government's failure to meet its public deficit goal. The deficit is now expected to reach 3.5 percent of gross domestic product compared with earlier projections of 2.5 percent.
-- HALF OF BRAZILIANS BACK IDEA OF DEMOCRACY, POLLS SHOW
Opinion polls show that Brazil is the South American country with the smallest percentage of inhabitants believing that democracy is the best form of government.
-- SHELL SEEKS 5.0 MLN-REAL RESTITUTION FROM SAO PAULO

Multinational oil firm Shell has gone to court to seek 5.0 million reais in restitution from the city of Sao Paulo for losses suffered during the 1989-1992 administration of former mayor Luisa Erundina.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
